gloss: feudal lord; lord of a domain

definitions.gloss: feudal lord; lord of a domain
definitions.explanation: A person who rules over a territory or domain, particularly in the context of feudal Japan or medieval Europe. The lord held authority over the land and its inhabitants.

examples.japanese: この{城|しろ}の{領主|りょうしゅ}は{武田氏|たけだし}だった。
examples.english: The lord of this castle was from the Takeda clan.

examples.japanese: {領主|りょうしゅ}は{農民|のうみん}から{年貢|ねんぐ}を{集|あつ}めた。
examples.english: The feudal lord collected annual tribute from the farmers.

examples.japanese: {戦国時代|せんごくじだい}には、{各地|かくち}の{領主|りょうしゅ}が{勢力|せいりょく}を{争|あらそ}い、{戦|いくさ}が{絶|た}えなかった。
examples.english: During the Warring States period, local lords competed for power and battles were constant.

notes:
USAGE:
{領主|りょうしゅ} is primarily a historical term used when discussing feudal systems in Japan and Europe.

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {大名|だいみょう} — a feudal lord of the Edo period, specifically a daimyo with land yielding at least 10,000 koku of rice
- {殿様|とのさま} — lord (respectful/familiar term, also used figuratively)
- {藩主|はんしゅ} — lord of a han (domain) in the Edo period
- {地主|じぬし} — landowner (modern, not feudal)

{領主|りょうしゅ} is more general than {大名|だいみょう} and can refer to lords of any era or country.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {領主|りょうしゅ}の{館|やかた} (the lord's manor)
- {領主|りょうしゅ}が{治|おさ}める (the lord governs)
- {領主|りょうしゅ}に{仕|つか}える (serve a lord)
